title: Chapter 67
content:
Blinking his eyes open, Jakyeong was greeted by the immediate sight of dark, sculpted brows and long, resting lashes.

Framed at point-blank range, the sharp, chiselled contours of Kang Il-hyun’s sleeping face were undeniably captivating. It was rare to observe the man in broad daylight with a sober, clear head. Peeling the heavy arm off his waist, Jakyeong slid out from beneath the duvet, reaching for his pack of cigarettes on the nightstand.

He slotted a filter between his lips and turned around—only to find Il-hyun already awake, watching him with a gentle, drowsy smile.

"Sleep well?"

The deep, sleep-laden baritone still carried a faint, lingering melancholy.

Il-hyun extended an open hand. Jakyeong scowled, shaking his head in an immediate, defensive refusal, which drew an amused chuckle from the mattress.

"Not for a hug. The cigarette."

Damn it. Jakyeong felt a sudden prickle of heat flush his neck, embarrassed that his mind had instinctively jumped to physical affection. He hastily tossed the lighter and a fresh smoke onto the sheets.

Il-hyun sat up, lighting the tip. The loose charcoal robe fell open across his chest, exposing broad, densely muscled pectorals. Exhaling a long ribbon of gray smoke against the morning light, his profile looked like a frame pulled straight from a classic neo-noir film.

Compared to Jakyeong’s lean, razor-sharp frame, Il-hyun possessed bold, heavy features. Jakyeong felt a quiet, reluctant pang of envy; the man simply looked naturally imposing and masculine.

At least my personality isn't completely rotten, Jakyeong consoled himself with a dry, internal scoff, taking a slow pull from his own smoke.

"What are your plans after wrapping up tomorrow's job?"

"Hard to say."

"If you're free... would you have dinner with me? Just the two of us."

It sounded unmistakably like asking someone out on a date. Jakyeong rolled the filter between his teeth, searching for the right words to defuse the invitation.

"If you'd rather not, you're free to decline," Il-hyun added smoothly.

The impeccably polite, gentlemanly tone felt completely alien. What on earth has gotten into this bastard since last night? Did commemorating his dead mother trigger a total spiritual reincarnation? The sudden absence of threats and foul language was intensely disorienting.

Seeing Il-hyun patiently awaiting a verdict, Jakyeong gave a noncommittal nod. "Tomorrow's schedule is packed. Let's do lunch the day after."

The corners of Il-hyun's lips curved into a handsome, radiant smile. "A date, then."

"In that case, could you head downstairs now? It'll be awkward if my brothers see you walking out of my room."

At the request, Il-hyun slid off the mattress without a single complaint. When he took a step toward Jakyeong, the boy tensed, stepping back—only for Il-hyun to glide right past him toward the hallway.

Resting a hand on the brass doorknob, Il-hyun looked back over his shoulder.

"Wash up and come down. Let's have breakfast together."

Flashing one last warm grin, he pulled the door shut behind him.

Jakyeong stood rooted to the hardwood, staring at the empty doorway in utter bewilderment. Is he genuinely being sincere? How does a sociopath flip his entire personality overnight? If this is an act, his temper should have cracked by now...

Unable to make sense of the madness, Jakyeong shook his head vigorously and padded into the en-suite bath to shower.

En route to the operational drop point, Jakyeong stared out the window.

The relentless summer rain showed no sign of letting up, keeping the city cloaked in a thick, suffocating humidity. It was the kind of grim weather that dragged a man's mood straight into the dirt—yet Kang Il-hyun had spent the last two days behaving like a docile lamb.

"About President Kang..." Wang Ryun spoke up from the front passenger seat, glancing back. "Doesn't he seem like a completely changed man?"

Wang Han gave a noncommittal shrug over the steering wheel. Ryun turned fully around to study Jakyeong's face, but received only stony silence.

"Did he actually fall head over heels for our Wei?"

Han drove a sharp elbow into Ryun’s ribs, warning him to drop the jokes. Jakyeong kept his eyes locked on the dripping side mirror, ignoring the banter entirely.

Tailing discreetly two car lengths behind their sedan was an unmarked black SUV.

Il-hyun’s private security detail. While billed as a tactical support cordon, everyone in the car knew it was primarily an escort to ensure they didn't skip the country mid-contract. Knowing the score, the three operatives chose to ignore the tail.

As the navigation approached the target coordinates, the chatter inside the cabin died into dead, operational silence.

The designated strike zone was an ultra-exclusive, members-only underground club in Gangnam—a fortified playground accessible only through biometric vetting and black-tier VIP credentials. Il-hyun had procured a legitimate membership pass for the breach.

Descending the access ramp, the surroundings triggered a sharp flash of deja vu; the district was the exact same nightlife strip Jakyeong had frequented with Kang Seok-joo a year ago.

The sedan rolled into the subterranean valet bay. Slipping on dark designer sunglasses, Jakyeong stepped out into the damp concrete garage, leaving Han and Ryun on mobile standby.

A suited host greeted him at the private elevator, guiding him through a labyrinthine sequence of mirrored hallways. At the security checkpoint, broad-shouldered bouncers were conducting thorough physical sweeps of incoming guests.

Jakyeong presented the black titanium card. A floor manager wearing an executive nametag offered a polished, mechanical bow.

"Our apologies, sir. To ensure absolute guest safety, comprehensive security screening is mandatory for all patrons. We appreciate your cooperation."

Jakyeong offered a polite nod.

A handheld metal detector swept down his torso and limbs. The wand gave a faint chirp over his luxury watch, which the guard cleared with a glance. Confirming zero concealed firearms or blades, they cleared him through the double doors.

THUMP. THUMP. THUMP.

Heavy, concussive bass rattled through the floorboards. Strobe arrays cut through the haze as a shirtless DJ worked the decks on the main stage. Flanking the sunken dance floor was an indoor glass pool, surrounded by high-society regulars casually smoking cannabis in broad daylight. The venue mirrored the illicit degenerate clubs Seok-joo favored in every detail.

Ascending the VIP staircase, a woman lounging in the pool caught Jakyeong's eye, raising her champagne flute in a suggestive toast. Jakyeong offered a thin smirk and continued up to the mezzanine.

Along the second-floor concourse, clusters of wealthy heirs were tangled on velvet sectionals, trading whispers and lines of powder.

According to the intelligence packet, the private suites along this corridor served as the primary distribution hub for high-grade synthetic narcotics, with the boutique hotel rooms upstairs facilitating high-end prostitution. Armed private guards stood posted outside key access doors, murmuring into their earpieces while tracking Jakyeong's movements with cold, professional caution.

Jakyeong leaned casually against the polished brass railing, surveying the floor below.

Twenty minutes later, a heavy security detail escorted a new entourage up the VIP stairs.

Behind his dark lenses, Jakyeong tracked the party with clinical focus. Dead-center in the formation was Choi Man-sik.

The man was noticeably broader than his file photographs—shaved bald, thick tribal ink crawling past his collar to his jawline, and a deep combat scar slicing across his cheek. The entourage marched straight past Jakyeong, heading into the fortified private room at the end of the hall.

As Jakyeong watched the door seal shut, a heavy hand clapped down onto his shoulder.

He spun around, his guard flaring—only to freeze in place.

It was Kang Seok-joo.

Seok-joo’s jaw dropped in pure, unadulterated shock before he lunged forward, wrapping Jakyeong in a loud, boisterous bear hug.

"Holy shit! Yi-an! What the fuck are the odds?!"

Jakyeong carefully pried the young heir off his chest, lowering his sunglasses down the bridge of his nose with a strained, awkward smile. Of all the places to run into this brat...

A heavy wave of top-shelf tequila rolled off Seok-joo's breath. A full year had passed, yet the kid hadn't matured a single day. Seok-joo waved his entourage ahead into their private booth, turning back to Jakyeong with wide, excited eyes.

"Man, it's been ages! When did you fly back into Seoul? Why didn't you hit me up?! You're not wearing your glasses—I almost walked right past you!"

Jakyeong forced a calm, delicate smile. "I slipped back into the country quietly without telling my family. I'd really appreciate it if you kept this between us."

Seok-joo clapped his arm with a conspiratorial grin. "Say no more. My lips are sealed."

"Thanks."

"Oh! Did you hear what happened after you left?!"

Rather than heading inside, Seok-joo launched into an animated, breathless gossip session. He recounted the assassination attempt at Il-hyun's inauguration in vivid detail, bitterly cursing the unknown sniper for having "dogshit aim"—bemoaning that the shooter should have put the round through Il-hyun's skull instead of giving him a survivable wound through the thighs.

Jakyeong wore a thin, bitter smile. My apologies, you little brat. Sorry for having dogshit aim.

Desperate to shake the kid before the target shifted positions, Jakyeong looked for an out.

Right on cue, the burner phone in his pocket began buzzing.

He pulled the device out, the caller ID flashing: The Bastard.

"Sorry, Seok-joo. I need to take this."

"No problem! Come hang out in Room 4 when you're done!" Seok-joo pointed down the hall before bouncing toward his booth.

Jakyeong hit accept, bringing the receiver to his ear as Il-hyun's smooth baritone broke the line.

[In the middle of the hit?]

Under normal circumstances, an unprompted operational check-in would have drawn a sharp scowl, but having just saved him from Seok-joo's endless chatter, the timing was remarkably welcome.

"Not yet."

[I called because there's something I was curious about.]

"Go ahead."

[What kind of flowers do you like?]

Jakyeong blinked. Calling in the middle of an active wet-work operation to ask for my favorite floral arrangement?

Before he could process the sheer absurdity of the question, Choi Man-sik stepped out of the private suite down the hall, flanked by two guards.

Jakyeong turned his back to the hall, tracking the reflection in the mirrored wall panel.

[Well?] Il-hyun pressed over the line. [Still thinking?]

"Uh... I don't really have a preference..." Jakyeong murmured into the mic, matching his pace to the target's movements.

Choi Man-sik dismissed his guards and pushed through the heavy doors of the executive restroom.

"I have to go," Jakyeong whispered, cutting the call.

He slipped into the restroom, throwing the heavy deadbolt on the main entrance. The marble sinks were vacant. Moving down the row of private stalls on silent soles, low, aggressive shouting echoed from the handicap suite at the far end.

Jakyeong slipped into the adjacent stall, locked the latch, and hoisted his shirt.

Wrapped snugly around his bare torso was a length of high-tensile braided tactical garrote wire, pre-knotted into a standard execution loop. He unwound the wire, stepping onto the porcelain toilet rim with fluid, weightless agility.

Over the partition, Man-sik was screaming into his diamond-encrusted phone:

"Fuck off! If you wanted the shipment, you should have wired the extra thirty percent! Russian scumbags think they can get top-tier supply for free—!"

In one blinding, explosive motion, Jakyeong dropped the reinforced loop over Choi Man-sik’s shaved head.

Man-sik’s eyes bulged as the braided wire clamped around his throat.

Jakyeong vaulted off the porcelain rim, dropping his full body weight to the floor while hauling the high-tensile wire taut across his shoulder.

GHK—! HRK!

Violent, strangled choking erupted from the stall as the steel cord bit deep into the target's windpipe.

Jakyeong braced his combat boots against the stall partition, wrapping the excess line around his forearms with bone-crushing leverage.

Despite the sudden asphyxiation, Man-sik’s massive frame possessed freakish brute strength. The man thrashed violently, slamming his massive back against the dividers with concussive, splintering crashes. The wire pulled so tight it threatened to slice through Jakyeong's leather gloves.

Suddenly—

SNAP.

The tension in the line gave out with a violent recoil.

CRASH!

The reinforced stall door was ripped off its hinges.

Jakyeong spun around, dropping the severed wire.

Standing in the doorway, bleeding from a deep laceration around his neck, was Choi Man-sik—wielding a serrated combat knife in his right hand, having sliced through the garrote wire mid-struggle.

Jakyeong clicked his tongue, taking two measured steps back into a tight defensive guard.

With bloodshot, manic eyes burning with pure, murderous frenzy, Choi Man-sik lunged forward with a feral roar:

"You dead little motherfucker!"
